skill.name: code-review-checklist
skill.description: Five-axis code review checklist (correctness, security, readability, performance, test coverage) producing actionable comments instead of style nitpicks. Use when the user asks to review code, a diff, or a pull request.
skill.summary: Review code across five quality areas with prioritized, line-specific comments and concrete fixes.
skill.author: alapha888

content.user_title: Review Code with a Five-Axis Checklist
content.value_statement: Unstructured code reviews can miss defects and spend time on style preferences. This skill guides five review areas and produces prioritized comments with concrete fixes.
actual_capabilities: Guide review across correctness, security, readability, performance, and test coverage.
Check edge cases, concurrency assumptions, and swallowed exceptions.
Inspect injection risks, hard-coded secrets, and sensitive logging.
Require concrete file and line references with suggested fixes for review comments.
Separate Must fix and Should fix comments, with a maximum of ten comments per review.
Request smaller reviews for diffs over approximately 400 changed lines and reject performance claims without evidence.
limitations: Provides review instructions, not an executable scanner or test runner.
Review accuracy depends on available code, requirements, and supporting context.
Large diffs require splitting, and the ten-comment limit can leave additional issues unlisted.
Merge-blocking guidance conflicts between correctness and security; teams must define their own approval policy.

use_cases.title: Check a change before submission
use_cases.description: Review a small diff for edge cases, security risks, and missing tests before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize team review comments
use_cases.description: Apply consistent review categories and priorities while keeping feedback tied to specific lines and concrete fixes.

use_cases.title: Evaluate unfamiliar contributions
use_cases.description: Review community changes for correctness, readability, and test coverage without focusing on formatting preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Review a function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this function using the five-axis checklist: [paste function with file name and line numbers]. Cite specific lines and suggest concrete fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small code sample.

prompt_templates.title: Review a pull request diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff: [paste diff]. Check scope first, then all five axes. Separate Must fix and Should fix comments. Use at most ten comments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before a pull request is approved.

prompt_templates.title: Review a sensitive change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authentication change: [paste diff and requirements]. Check correctness, injection risks, secrets, logging, and remaining axes. Cite evidence and identify missing edge-case tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of security-sensitive application logic.

prompt_templates.title: Review with supporting evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff with requirements, tests, and profiling results: [attach context]. Mark each axis pass, fail, or N-A. Prioritize concrete fixes within ten comments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review combining code, tests, and measured performance.

output_examples.input: A small order-processing diff indexes the first order without checking whether the list is empty.
output: Must fix | Correctness | order.py:87: An empty order list causes IndexError. Check for an empty list before accessing its first item.
Should fix | Test coverage | order.py:87: Add an empty-order test to cover the failing path.

output_examples.input: A contributor requests review of a diff containing 650 changed lines.
output_examples.output: Scope: The diff exceeds approximately 400 changed lines. Split it into smaller, focused changes before review.

output_examples.input: A reviewer suspects a loop is slow but provides no measurements or evidence of repeated work.
output_examples.output: Performance: No evidence found to support a performance finding. Do not raise a speculative performance comment.

best_practices: Provide the diff, file names, line numbers, and relevant requirements.
Split changes over approximately 400 lines into focused reviews.
Require evidence and a concrete fix for each comment, and clarify team merge-blocking rules.
anti_patterns: Approve a change without reading the complete diff.
Spend review comments on formatting preferences instead of substantive defects.
Report vague problems or performance concerns without code references and evidence.

faq.question: What does the checklist cover?
faq.answer: It covers correctness, security, readability, performance, and test coverage, in that order.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests or security scans?
faq.answer: No. It supplies review guidance and examples, not test execution or scanning tools.

faq.question: How large should a review be?
faq.answer: The skill asks for a split when a diff exceeds approximately 400 changed lines.

faq.question: How many comments should a review contain?
faq.answer: The limit is ten comments. When problems exceed that limit, the guidance recommends requesting a rewrite.

faq.question: Does it review formatting preferences?
faq.answer: No. It leaves indentation, quote choices, and semicolons to linters.

faq.question: Which findings block a merge?
faq.answer: The guidance is inconsistent: correctness alone blocks in one section, while security also requires fixes in another. Define your team policy explicitly.
